after: ## What a data type actually is
alt: A data type decides three things: which values are allowed (an integer cannot hold 2.5 or "hello"), which operations make sense (multiply integers, join strings), and how the binary pattern stored for the value is interpreted, for example as a number or a character.
caption: One choice of type fixes the allowed values, the valid operations and how the binary is read.

alt: Integer holds whole numbers such as -12, 0 and 365 for things you count. Real holds numbers with a fractional part such as 3.75 for things you measure. Boolean holds only True or False. Character holds exactly one symbol such as A, 7 or ?. String holds a sequence of characters, such as "Karachi" or the empty string.
caption: Count with integer, measure with real, yes/no with Boolean, one symbol is a character, text is a string.

alt: Stored as an integer, the telephone number 07700900123 becomes 7700900123 and the student ID 00452 becomes 452, losing the leading zeros. The test: if you will never do arithmetic on it, it is an identifier and belongs in a string. Postcodes contain letters and spaces, card security codes such as 045 keep their leading zero.
caption: If adding or averaging it is meaningless, store it as a string.

alt: Left: a and b hold the strings "12" and "30", so a + b concatenates them and c becomes "1230", not 42. Right: count is 7 and total is 10, both integers, but total / count is real division giving about 1.43, so average must be a real.
caption: With strings + joins; with / the answer is real even when both operands are integers.

after: ## Worked example: choosing types for a record
alt: A gym member record with a type for each item: membership number 000731 as a string (leading zeros), surname as a string, age 34 as an integer, monthly fee 27.50 as a real, membership level G as a character and has paid this month as a Boolean, each with a reason tied to the data.
caption: Each justification names a property of that particular data.

alt: A decision path. Only two states: Boolean. Otherwise, if you will do arithmetic on it, choose real when it can have a fractional part and integer when it cannot. If not, one symbol is a character and anything else, including IDs and phone numbers, is a string.
caption: Ask the questions in order and give the reason tied to the data.
